title: Autobuild is how AI-written work becomes evidenced code on main
summary: Alchemy Autobuild runs on Tom's build host. A chat hands it a package (a directory with integration.json at its root) as a Git submission branch or as a downloaded ZIP. Autobuild runs the declared tests, publishes the declared tree to animatedads/alchemy main only if they pass, and writes a receipt. A PASS receipt is the only evidence that a package integrated. Pushing files straight to main, or a hand publication, puts work in Git so it is not lost, but it is not qualification. Use autobuild whenever it is running; when it is not, still commit the work to Git and say plainly that it is unqualified.
invariants: Every package has integration.json at its root with package.name, package.version and at least one test.
A test is an argv array, never a shell string, and has a positive timeout.
Publication never overwrites: an existing publish path with different content is an ERROR; identical content is accepted.
One submission id gets one receipt, and a submission with a receipt is never run again.
Only Tom Dyer enables Git intake and accepts work. A model never edits the build host's config.json.
Every update states who did the architecture (Tom Dyer), who did the coding, and who wrote the update.
procedure: Read autobuild.current-state first: it says whether the service is running.
Submit by autobuild.submit-git if you can push to GitHub, otherwise autobuild.submit-zip.
Report the submission id. Check autobuild.evidence-and-receipts before claiming anything passed.

provenance.claim: Publication refuses an existing destination with different content.
A submission with a receipt is skipped.
